subject: Competitive eval follow-up: model quality comparisons & next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps from today's discovery (redwood vs hyperscalers)

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the clear context on Acme's fraud-detection use case and the latency/cost targets you're tracking. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Traffic: ~200 req/s peak for inference, 50 req/s steady state with bursts.
- Quality bar: <2% false positives, hallucination incidents must be <0.5% on sample prompts.
- Constraints: PCI-scope data, need audit logs and tenant isolation (potentially Private).
- Current contenders: Anthropic + Anthropic API, OpenAI + Azure, and internal evals on AWS Sagemaker endpoints.

Where Redwood stands (short):
- Model quality: we recommend running a head-to-head on your seed prompts (we can run on the same prompts + temperature configs).
- Production economics: continuous batching + prefix cache typically reduces per-token cost by 30-60% vs naive single-request endpoints.
- Deployment flexibility: hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem) options to meet PCI/contractual needs.

Proposed next tests (what we'd like to run together):
1) Model quality sweep: run your seed prompts through Redwood-served models, OpenAI, and Anthropic with matched decoding params. Track hallucination rate, answer correctness, and regression on historical prompts.
2) Stress/latency run: synthetic traffic at 50 / 200 req/s with realistic prompt lengths. Measure p50/p95/p99 latency and tail behaviors.
3) Token-cost model: run a 24-hour sampled workload to estimate monthly cost delta with and without caching/batching.
4) Security checklist: share SOC2 evidence + network access checklist for Private deployment.

Attachments: I attached the seed prompts CSV we discussed and a quick comparison sheet (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-quicksheet.pdf). Also attaching the demo recording.

Next steps / asks:
- Sam: can you confirm the preferred test window next week?
- Priya: please share the procurement timeline and any specific contract/IL constraints we should prep for.
- Rishi: will you/Dev be available to run the stress testing with our infra engineers?

I'll put together a short mutual action plan once we lock the test window. Happy to jump on a 30-min sync to walk through the test definitions.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — useful summary.

Quick answers:
- Test window: we're good for Wed 16th (PDT) or Thu 17th AM. Prefer Wed afternoon if your team can run the stress tests.
- Procurement: Priya will lead; target decision by end of April but we have to get security signoff first.
- Success metrics: for the model quality sweep we'll use your suggested metrics + a short list we maintain: hallucination rate, FPR on labeled set, average response time on production-ish prompts.

One ask: can you provide the exact eval harness you will run (script/params) so we can reproduce on our side for Anthropic/OpenAI runs? Also send a short doc that defines how hallucination is measured (examples/thresholds).

Hey Sam,

Thanks — quick technical notes on the eval harness and what we'll need from Acme: 
- We'll share a reproducible harness (python + simple YAML config) that will: iterate your seed prompts, call each provider with matched params, and log outputs + model metadata (model id, temperature, tokens).
- For hallucination measurement we'll require a label file (CSV) with expected-safe answers for the test set or an oracle scoring function. If you can't provide labels for all prompts, we can run a sampled human review.
- To run stress tests we need access to a test endpoint (we can provide a sandbox key) and a sample payload distribution (prompt length hist, token distribution).

Note on security: for PCI scope we recommend starting with Redwood Private (VPC) for the initial POC. We can also run a hosted test with redacted data if you prefer to avoid early network setup. For audit logs and KMS we'd need to setup a short checklist before the Private deployment test.

I'll attach a link to the harness repo and a short README after this note.

— Dev
